arxiv-2010-03970.title: Quantum Nuclei at Weakly Bonded Interfaces: The Case of Cyclohexane on Rh(111)
arxiv-2010-03970.creator: Karen Fidanyan, Ikutaro Hamada, Mariana Rossi
arxiv-2010-03970.description: Abstract The electronic properties of interfaces can depend on their isotopic constitution. One known case is that of cyclohexane physisorbed on Rh(111), in which isotope effects have been measured on the work function change and desorption energies. These effects can only be captured by calculations including nuclear quantum effects (NQE).

arxiv-2104-11478.title: Inductive biases and Self Supervised Learning in modelling a physical heating system
arxiv-2104-11478.creator: Cristian Vicas
arxiv-2104-11478.description: Abstract Model Predictive Controllers (MPC) require a good model for the controlled process. In this paper I infer inductive biases about a physical system. I use these biases to derive a new neural network architecture that can model this real system that has noise and inertia.

arxiv-2110-03333.title: Future Constraints on Primordial Black Holes from XGIS-THESEUS
arxiv-2110-03333.creator: Diptimoy Ghosh, Divya Sachdeva, Praniti Singh
arxiv-2110-03333.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Diptimoy Ghosh, Divya Sachdeva, Praniti Singh. Current observations allow Primordial Black Holes (PBHs) in asteroid mass range 10 17 − 10 22 10^{17}-10^{22} g to constitute the entire dark matter (DM) energy density (barring a small mass range constrained by 21 cm observations).

arxiv-2208-02451.title: Three-Dimensional Structure of the Central Molecular Zone 2020
arxiv-2208-02451.creator: Yoshiaki Sofue
arxiv-2208-02451.description: Abstract A detailed comparison of HI and CO line cube data of the Galactic Center (GC) region from the archives is obtained. The central molecular zone (CMZ) is shown to be embedded in the HI disc (central HI zone, CHZ) of radius ∼ 320 \sim 320 pc and vertical scale height ∼ 70 \sim 70 pc.

arxiv-2403-11779.title: Home Spaces and Invariants to Analyze Parameterized Petri Nets
arxiv-2403-11779.creator: Gerard Memmi
arxiv-2403-11779.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Gerard Memmi. This article focuses on comparing the notions of home spaces and invariants, in Transition Systems and more particularly, in Petri Nets as well as a variety of derived Petri Nets. After recalling basic notions of Petri Nets and semiflows, we then discuss important characteristics of finite generating sets for ℱ \mathcal{F} , the set of all semiflows with integer coordinates of a given Petri Net. Then, we particularly focus on ℱ + \mathcal{F^{+}} the set of semiflows with non-negative coordinates.

arxiv-2602-06347.title: Validation of a high-order finite difference compressible solver
arxiv-2602-06347.creator: Yujoo Kang, Sang Lee
arxiv-2602-06347.description: Abstract The verification and validation of a high-order compressible in-house solver based on a compact finite difference scheme are presented. Validation is performed using five canonical cases: the one-dimensional Sod shock tube problem, two-dimensional shock–shear layer interaction, compressible channel flow, compressible turbulent boundary layer, and shock-turbulent boundary layer interaction.

britannica-1911-plock-government.creator: Encyclopaedia Britannica
britannica-1911-plock-government.description: Article 'Plock (government)' from the 1911 Encyclopædia Britannica (Volume 21), the classic English-language general encyclopedia, now in the public domain. West and East Prussia on the N. and the Polish governments of Lomza on the E. Its flat surface, 350 to 500 ft. above the sea-level, rises gently towards the north, where it merges into the Baltic coast-ridge of the Prussian lake district. Only a few hills reach 600 ft. above the sea, while the broad valley of the Vistula has an elevation of only 130 to 150 ft.

pmc-11384815.title: Genetic issues in ICP
pmc-11384815.creator: Julia Zöllner, Catherine Williamson, Peter H Dixon, WM “Bill” Hague, Charlotte Frise, Stephen Lapinsky
pmc-11384815.description: Intrahepatic cholestasis of pregnancy (ICP) is the commonest gestational liver disorder with variable global incidence. Genetic susceptibility, combined with hormonal and environmental influences, contributes to ICP aetiology. Adverse pregnancy outcomes linked to elevated serum bile acids highlight the importance of comprehensive risk assessment. ABCB4 and ABCB11 gene variants play a significant role in about 20% of severe ICP cases.

pmc-11630590.title: Assessing species composition and insecticide resistance of Anopheles gambiae complex members in three coastal health districts of Côte d’Ivoire
pmc-11630590.creator: Jackson K. I. Kouamé, Constant V. A. Edi, Julien B. Z. Zahouli, Ruth M. A. Kouamé, Yves A. K. Kacou, Firmain N. Yokoly, Constant G. N. Gbalegba, David Malone, Benjamin G. Koudou, Luca Nelli, Luca Nelli, Luca Nelli, Luca Nelli
pmc-11630590.description: Although malaria is endemic in coastal Côte d’Ivoire, updated data on the resistance profile of the main vector, Anopheles gambiae sensu lato (s.l.), are still lacking, thus compromising decision-making for an effective vector control intervention. This study investigated the complex members and the insecticide resistance in the Anopheles gambiae s.l. populations in coastal Côte d’Ivoire.

pmc-12485551.title: Facing the possibility of consciousness in human brain organoids
pmc-12485551.creator: Christopher Wood, Hao Wang, Wei-Jun Yang, Yongmei Xi
pmc-12485551.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). SummaryHuman brain organoids (HBOs) have emerged as transformative models for neurodevelopment and disease, yet ethical concerns persist regarding their potential to develop consciousness. Since 2020, a growing cohort of neuroscientists and philosophers has dismissed these concerns as unscientific, citing limited structural complexity, absence of bodily integration and environmental interaction, and a prevailing neuroscientific consensus against the feasibility of any, or any near-future, emergence of HBO consciousness, thus challenging any suggested revisions of ethical guidelines and safeguards.

pmc-12969091.title: Stakeholder views on the installation and use of mile long tracks in community parks aimed at increasing physical activity in low-income minority areas: A qualitative evaluation in Birmingham UK.

pmc-12969091.description: ObjectivesPhysical activity (PA) is essential for preventing and managing chronic diseases and improving mental health. Despite national guidelines recommending regular PA, significant disparities exist across demographic groups and regions in the UK, with Birmingham and the West Midlands reporting some of the lowest activity levels.

pmc-13031719.title: Enhancing reliability and spectral efficiency in future wireless networks via intelligent omni-surface enhanced MU-MIMO cooperative hybrid NOMA
pmc-13031719.creator: Helen Sheeba John Kennedy, Vinoth Babu Kumaravelu, Poongundran Selvaprabhu, Arthi Murugadass, Sellam Viruthagiri
pmc-13031719.description: The growing demand for high-capacity next-generation networks drives the need for efficient and scalable multiple access schemes. This study proposes a unified integrated analytical framework for intelligent omni-surface (IOS)-enhanced multi-user MIMO cooperative hybrid NOMA (MU-MIMO-C-HNOMA) system employing maximal ratio transmission (MRT) at the gNodeB (gNB) to enhance reliability, throughput, and sum spectral efficiency (SSE).

pmc-13045103.title: Meta-analyses in sport and exercise science: sometimes the right tool at the wrong time?
pmc-13045103.creator: Sebastian Puschkasch-Möck, José Afonso, Konstantin Warneke, Klaus Wirth
pmc-13045103.description: BackgroundMeta-analysis is widely regarded as a high-level form of evidence in scientific research, particularly in the medical and life sciences. In sport and exercise science, the number of published meta-analyses has increased rapidly in recent years. This expansion raises important questions about when quantitative synthesis is appropriate and when meta-analysis may become the right tool at the wrong time.

pmc-13080386.title: The taxonomic status and range distribution of Boulenophrys shuichengensis (Anura, Megophryidae)
pmc-13080386.creator: Dongru Zhang, Lu Chen, Rongchuan Xiong, Wenjing Shen, Felista Kasyoka Kilunda, Weiwei Pan, Miao Zhong, Jianhong Li, Yunhe Wu
pmc-13080386.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). BackgroundBoulenophrys shuichengensis (Tian & Sun, 1995) has for a long time been a subject of taxonomic ambiguity due to rare field records and a lack of molecular data from its type locality.New informationTo address this, we integrated molecular, morphological and type locality survey data: three tadpoles were collected from the type locality and seven adult males from Weixin County, Yunnan Province, China.

pmc-13275704.title: MGST1 drives lymph node metastasis in papillary thyroid carcinoma via mitochondrial metabolic reprogramming and immune suppression
pmc-13275704.creator: Qing-Xuan Wang, Chang-Feng Yu, Ke-Chen Zhang, Jun-Hao Zhang, Xu-Jie Zhou, Tong-Xin Zou, Hao-Zhuo Huang, Tian-Yu Han, Hua-Zhen Mei, Kai-Bo Su, Jie You, Jin-Miao Qu, Cong Xie, Quan Li, Ye-Feng Cai
pmc-13275704.description: BackgroundWhile papillary thyroid carcinoma (PTC) generally exhibits a favorable prognosis, a subset of patients experiences poorer outcomes, with lymph node metastasis (LNM) significantly increasing the risk of recurrence and correlating with a worse prognosis. Mitochondrial metabolic reprogramming and immune evasion play pivotal roles in driving lymph node metastasis; however, the specific actionable targets within these processes remain largely unexplored.

pmc-13321683.title: A novel Chimeric Antigen Receptor (CAR) - strategy to target EGFRVIII-mutated glioblastoma cells via macrophages
pmc-13321683.creator: Kristi Vera, Gülen Esken, Jin Wook Hwang, Carine Elbaz, Diana Chaker, Noufissa Oudrhiri, Christophe Desterke, Frank Griscelli, Annelise Bennaceur-Griscelli, Ali G Turhan
pmc-13321683.description: BackgroundAutologous chimeric antigen receptor (CAR) expressing T-Cells (CAR-T) have been efficiently used in hematological malignancies but their efficacy in solid tumors remains limited. CAR therapies via the use of macrophages, offer a promising avenue due to their unique ability to infiltrate tumors and to initiate phagocytosis.
